title: Planning Fallacy
equation: Realistic Estimate = Inside-View Estimate × Outside-View Multiplier
hook: Everything takes longer than you think. Even when you plan for it taking longer.
statement: People almost always underestimate how long things will take and how much they'll cost.
explainer: Your gut plans for the best case. Big projects run late and over budget because planners only look at their own plan. Check how similar past projects really went, then adjust.
sop: Estimate the task from the bottom up.
Find 5 or more similar past projects.
See how much they actually overran.
Add a buffer for surprises you can't predict.
equation_example: Your Inside-View Estimate is 4 weeks. Your last 5 launches ran 1.5 times over, so the Outside-View Multiplier is 1.5. 4 × 1.5 = 6 weeks. A higher multiplier means you need bigger buffers. Near 1.0 means your gut is reliable.
question: Look up your last three projects and write how long each took versus what you planned.
closing_statement: Your gut estimate is a starting bid, not a promise.
caption:
Principle Nº 298: Planning Fallacy

Everything takes longer than you think. Even when you plan for it taking longer.

People almost always underestimate how long things will take and how much they'll cost.

Your turn: Look up your last three projects and write how long each took versus what you planned.
